glance-intake.png.name: glance-intake.png
glance-intake.png.textSnippet: You should see a Shark, a Fish and a score stuck on 0. The little pictures at the bottom right are the game's SPRITES — a sprite is one character or thing in the game. Click a sprite and you will see
glance-intake.png.contentAnchor: You should see a Shark, a Fish and a score stuck on 0. The little pictures at the bottom right are the game's SPRITES — a sprite is one character or thing in the game. Click a sprite and you will see its SCRIPTS: the stacks of blocks that tell that sprite what to do. Every sprite carries its OWN scripts, never anyone else's — that is why a bug can hide on one sprite while everything else looks fine. One more word you WILL meet on the Fish: CLONE. A clone is a temporary copy of a sprite that Scratch makes while the game runs — every fish swimming in the water is a clone of the one Fish sprite in the list. Most of the bugs are hiding in the sprites' scripts — but not all of them: one case will take you somewhere new.
glance-intake.png.says: Evidence Intake — four steps to get the broken game open

04-case.jpg.contentAnchor: Open the Shark's scripts and compare them with each other. Working code is your best evidence: what does every WORKING arrow script start with that the broken one is missing? Cannot see all five stacks at once? glance-jellyfish.png.textSnippet: Add a Jellyfish from Scratch's sprite library: click 'Choose a Sprite' at the bottom right, then search 'Jellyfish'. Build it with the starter blocks in the picture below: the jellyfish drifts to a ne
glance-jellyfish.png.contentAnchor: Add a Jellyfish from Scratch's sprite library: click 'Choose a Sprite' at the bottom right, then search 'Jellyfish'. Build it with the starter blocks in the picture below: the jellyfish drifts to a new spot every couple of seconds, and if the Shark ever touches it, the whole game stops. That 'if touching' block is next lesson's superpower — this is a sneak preview. Finished the jellyfish and want more? Design ONE more change of your own — a second danger, a speed-up, a power-up — and name it in your release note.
